goal: Ship the recipient-facing opt-out path: the RFC 8058 Railway ingress and the /u/<token> landing page that redeem an Unsubscribe token into a scope='global' Suppression ledger row.
non_goals: Unsubscribe token MINTING — owned by #630 (B4); this ticket only redeems and exports the hash function #630 will import
Any migration — 096 created both tables and 097 registered both analytics event names
Eager cancel of pending asks (§6.2) — that would make an unauthenticated public endpoint perform a cross-account fan-out write on the one route that must never be rate-limited
Admin or owner suppression surfaces (#645) and the §8.2 Correction path
A job_outbox row (§9.3) — there is no follow-up work to make transactional with
An inbound_events dedup claim on the ingress — idempotency already comes from first-write-wins plus redeemed_at, and a second write would complicate the commit-then-2xx contract for no gain
Rate limiting, BotID registration, or WAF enforcement on either path (§9.2)
user_visible_behavior: POST /ingress/unsubscribe/<token> on Railway writes a global Suppression ledger row with source='unsubscribe_one_click' and returns 200 only after the transaction commits
GET /ingress/unsubscribe/<token> 302s to ${NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL}/u/<token> for clients that treat the List-Unsubscribe header as a link
GET /u/<token> renders a no-login, no-fee, no-form-fields page with one prominent button, naming the originating business, and writes nothing
Submitting that button POSTs to /api/u/<token>, which writes source='unsubscribe_link' and 303s to /u/<token>?ok=<signed receipt> — the receipt is minted server-side only after the write commits

GET /u/<token>?ok=<receipt> renders the success copy — the generic 'the business that contacted you' sentence, naming NO business — only when the receipt verifies against the token hash and is within its 10-minute TTL; it writes nothing. An absent, malformed, forged or expired receipt (including a hand-crafted ?done=1) falls through to the button page or the neutral page and NEVER renders success
Unknown, malformed, and already-redeemed tokens all render one identical neutral page carrying the mailto: fallback

An unknown or malformed token at the ingress returns 503 with deliberately NO Sentry event and NO per-request log line — it is counted into a 60s aggregate — so the provider retries and a #630 mint-race is still recoverable without giving scanner traffic an unbounded telemetry path; an unknown token at POST /api/u/<token> 303s to the bare neutral page rather than claiming a success that did not happen
Every path above keeps working with SOLICITATION_SEND_ENABLED off (DR1)
invariants: Invariant #5 — the raw Unsubscribe token is never persisted or logged; only its SHA-256 hash is compared
Invariant #1 — the Next.js routes do a Postgres write only; no LLM, external, or long-running work
Invariant #6 — the third-party provider POST terminates on Railway, not proxied through Next.js
Invariant #13 — SOLICITATION_UNSUBSCRIBE_MAILTO is server-only with no NEXT_PUBLIC_* companion
Invariant #15 — the redemption module takes tx as an explicit parameter; only the route handler and the ingress handler (composition roots) import the db singleton
§9.1 — 2xx only after the ledger write commits; a write failure is 5xx plus a loud Sentry report, deliberately NOT log-and-swallow
§9.2 — neither path is rate-limited, BotID-protected, or WAF-enforced
§9.5 — never log the raw handle or the raw token; a token_hash prefix or row id only
DR1 — no suppression-path code reads SOLICITATION_SEND_ENABLED
§5.4 — unknown, malformed, and redeemed tokens are indistinguishable to the caller (enumeration resistance)
§5.2 — a token whose account was purged still writes a ledger row, unconditionally, with account_id NULL
§5.5 — the button page names exactly one business and never any other account; the success page names none (deliberate deviation, see edge cases)
§2.1 first-write-wins — redemption never overwrites an earlier suppression row and never writes a duplicate
edge_cases: A provider re-POSTs the same token: 200 no-op, no duplicate row, no error
The handle is already suppressed by a different source (e.g. complaint): first-write-wins leaves the earlier row alone and redemption still reports success
The token's account was purged: account_id/business_id/ask_id are NULL, the ledger row is still written with account_id NULL, and the page falls back to generic copy

Unknown or malformed token at the ingress: 503, NO Sentry event and NO per-request log line (counted into the 60s aggregate instead) — the provider retries, so a token minted in a transaction that commits after the ask is delivered is still redeemable (round-1 finding 1; telemetry bounded per owner-run review finding 2)
Unknown token at POST /api/u/<token>: 303s to the bare neutral-page URL with NO receipt minted — a compliance page must not claim an opt-out that did not happen

A percent-encoded ingress path (/ingress/%75nsubscribe/<token>) resolves to the unsubscribe route and must ALSO escape the rate limiter — a raw-string prefix test fails this, so the exclusion keys on resolved route config, not on URL text (finding 2)
An unmatched path under the unsubscribe prefix (/ingress/unsubscribe/x/extra) 404s and must STAY rate-limited, so the exclusion cannot open an unthrottled flood namespace (finding 2)

The ledger write throws: the adapter catches it, reports a sanitized exception to Sentry, and returns 503 itself — the raw token must never reach Fastify's default error handler, whose pino serializer logs request.url (finding 3, invariant #5)
Two overlapping redemptions of one token: exactly one ledger row, exactly one redeemed_at, and the loser must not overwrite the winner's timestamp (finding 4)
A token whose handle was already suppressed by a complaint: recordSuppression returns null, but redeemed_at must STILL be stamped — otherwise the token stays redeemable forever (finding 4)
A token whose business_id belongs to a different account than its account_id (minting bug): the page must fall back to generic copy, never name that business (finding 5)

A token containing reserved characters (a%2Fb decodes to a/b): every path construction must encodeURIComponent, or the redirect becomes a two-segment path that 404s instead of reaching the neutral page (finding 6)
SOLICITATION_UNSUBSCRIBE_MAILTO unset: the neutral page omits the mailto line rather than rendering a broken one
SOLICITATION_SEND_ENABLED off: ingress, landing page, and every ledger write stay fully live (DR1)
Provider POST carries application/x-www-form-urlencoded body 'List-Unsubscribe=One-Click': parsed by the existing app-wide parser, contents ignored and never required

The global /ingress/ rate-limit onRequest hook must not fire for the resolved unsubscribe routes (POST, GET and inherited HEAD) while still firing for every other ingress path — including percent-encoded spellings of the ingress root such as /%69ngress/resend, which resolve correctly but defeat a raw-URL prefix test — and for unmatched 404 paths under the prefix
The ledger write throws: 503 plus a sanitized Sentry event, never a 2xx — Sentry is reserved for genuine infra failure, which is rare and self-bounding, unlike unknown-token traffic
Cross-site form POST to /api/u/<token>: accepted by design — a token can only suppress the handle it already belongs to (§9.2)
business_id is non-null but the businesses row is gone: generic fallback copy, not an error

§5.5 vs §5.4 conflict, resolved at plan time: rendering §5.5's named-business sentence on the receipt-gated success page would require resolving a now-redeemed token, making it distinguishable from an unknown one on that URL. §5.4 wins — the button page carries the business name, the success page uses the generic sentence, and the module exports ONE lookup that collapses unknown/malformed/redeemed to null

A hand-crafted /u/<anything>?done=1 or a forged/expired ?ok= receipt: renders the button page or the neutral page, NEVER the success copy — the success view is bound to a server-minted HMAC receipt, not to the presence of a query parameter (owner-run adversarial review, finding 1)
Hostile or scanner traffic hammering unknown tokens: at most ONE aggregated warn line per 60-second window per process, never one per request (owner-run adversarial review, finding 2)

Worker restarts mid-window: the partial unknown-token count is flushed by the graceful shutdown sequence; an ungraceful crash loses at most one 60s window, which is acceptable for a rate signal and feeds no correctness decision

A spent token replayed AFTER an audited Correction-path removal: redeemed_at IS NOT NULL proves only that it was once redeemed, NOT that a suppression exists. The ledger is checked explicitly; with no live global row the outcome is already_redeemed_not_suppressed -> no receipt, neutral page, and deliberately NO re-suppression (owner-run review round 2, finding 1)

Hostile traffic against the limiter-exempt route: a 1 KB per-route body limit and a bounded-concurrency bulkhead returning 503 + Retry-After keep it from saturating the shared worker/DB pool. A bulkhead DEFERS with a retryable status; a rate limiter DROPS -- only the latter is forbidden by 9.2 (owner-run review round 2, finding 2)

rollback_plan: Revert the PR. There is no migration to reverse — 096 created both tables and 097 registered both analytics event names, and this ticket adds neither. Suppression ledger rows written before the revert are recipient opt-outs and MUST be kept; nothing in the rollback deletes them. SOLICITATION_UNSUBSCRIBE_MAILTO can be left set or unset with no effect once the code is gone. The real cost of a revert is that already-delivered asks advertise URLs that would 404, which is why this rides staging first and the revert window must be short.
observability: One structured [ingress/unsubscribe] log line per request for outcomes redeemed | already_suppressed | failed, carrying a token_hash prefix — never the handle, never the raw token. UNKNOWN tokens are deliberately EXCLUDED from per-request logging: the route is exempt from the global ingress limiter (§9.2), so a scanner sweep or provider retry storm would otherwise be an unbounded log-ingestion path. They are counted instead and emitted as at most ONE line per 60s per process, tagged with replica_id so counts sum correctly across a cross-deployment replica overlap, flushed on graceful shutdown

A loud Sentry error on ledger write failure ONLY — the §9.1 signal. Unknown tokens deliberately emit NO Sentry event: the route is unauthenticated and unrate-limited by §9.2, worker Sentry has no error sampling or dedup, and scanner traffic would otherwise become unbounded event volume

The solicitation_suppressed analytics event already emitted by recordSuppression, whose source property splits unsubscribe_one_click (RFC 8058, unattended) from unsubscribe_link (human click) so the two channels are measurable separately
A rising unknown-outcome rate at the ingress is the earliest evidence that #630's token minting is broken — a token we advertised but cannot resolve
